Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia
Bench: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia
 1 Mcrc No.12990/2024
In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia
 On The 3rd Of April, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 12990 of 2024
Between:-
1. Kapil Gupta S/O Shri Gurudayal Gupta,
 Aged About 37 Years, Occupation: Business
 Resident Of 274 Ward No.11, Mukharji
 Nagar, Raisen, Tehsil And District Raisen
 (Madhya Pradesh)
2. Guru Dayal Gupta S/O Late Shri Nandan
 Prasad Gupta, Aged About 69 Years,
 Occupation: Retired Official, Resident Of
 274 Ward No.11, Mukharji Nagar, Raisen,

 Housewife Resident Of 274 Ward No.11,
 Mukharji Nagar, Raisen, Tehsil And

4. Rahul Gupta S/O Shri Gurudayal Gupta,
 Aged About 41 Years, Occupation: Business
 Resident Of 274 Ward No.11, Mukharji
 Nagar, Raisen, Tehsil And District Raisen
 (Madhya Pradesh)

the following:
 Order
This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking the following reliefs:
I. To quash the impugned FIR No.10/2024 dated 28.02.2024/Annexure A-8.
registered by respondent no.1; and II. to award cost. 
2. It is submitted by counsel for applicants that respondent No.2 lodged an FIR to the effect that she got married to applicant No.1 on 28.11.2019 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals. Her parents had given sufficient dowry as well as cash amount of Rs.2,00,000/-. For 5 days after her marriage she was kept properly. When she again went back to her matrimonial house then applicants started quarrelling and abusing her on the ground of household works and in case if any mistake is committed by her then her mother-in-law used to turn her out of the matrimonial house. Her mother-in-law was not giving food to eat and was also in habit of assaulting her. When she narrated the incident to her husband then he too was scolding that she should remain silent and he was also in habit of assaulting her on trivial issues. He used to threaten her to give divorce. Her elder brother-in-law (Jaith) also used to abuse her filthily. Her mobile was snatched by applicants. In the month of March, 2020 on the occasion of Holi festival she came back to her parental home. 
Thereafter, when she went back to her matrimonial house, then applicants enquired as to whether she has brought anything or not? They also scolded that her parents had assured that they would give a four-wheeler, then why she has not brought a four-wheeler. When respondent No.2 stated that her father is no more and her marriage was performed by her maternal grandfather therefore she can insist upon four-wheeler. Thereafter, her maternal grandfather also expired during COVID-19. Her mobile was also snatched and therefore, she was not able to talk to her mother. The applicants were always insisting that she should bring a four-wheeler and should also ask for her share in the property of her maternal grandfather. On account of atrocities, she came back to her parental home. Her husband filed an application under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act before Family Court, Raisen in which a compromise took place. Thereafter, she resided in her matrimonial house for 4 months but applicants were continuously passing taunts on account of less dowry and on the ground that she has not conceived so far. Accordingly, it was alleged that all the applicants Kapil Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25534528/
2 are harassing her and treating her with cruelty on account of demand of four-wheeler as well as on account of household issues. Since she was not intending to spoil her marital life, therefore, earlier she did not lodge the report. 
3. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that FIR was lodged on 28.02.2024. In the proceedings under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, mediation had taken place on 12.06.2023 and in that mediation proceedings respondent No.2 did not make any allegation of cruelty. Even while dismissing the proceedings under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage act, Trial Court has also not referred to any atrocity or cruelty committed by applicants. Respondent No.2 thereafter had made one more complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Narsinghpur on 16.01.2024 in which similar allegations were made. It is submitted that if FIR is accepted on its own face value, then it is clear that FIR is barred by time. The allegations are vague and omnibus and are general in nature. To buttress her contentions, counsel for applicants has relied upon the judgments passed by Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar Alias Sonam and others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599 and Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another, reported in (2012) 4 SCC 379.
4. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for State. It is submitted that there are specific allegations of cruelty on account of demand of dowry. On earlier occasions also respondent No.2 had made complaints. 
5. Heard learned counsel for parties.
6. Applicant No.1 had filed an application under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act. It is the contention of his counsel that when reconciliation proceedings took place, respondent No.2 did not disclose the details of cruelty committed by applicants and therefore, the allegations made in the FIR are false. 
7. In the considered opinion of this Court, the said submission cannot be accepted. When parties have decided to forgive each other and to restart their marriage life then it was not expected from the mediator to reproduce the entire allegations which compelled respondent No.2 to reside separately. Making the life of a lady miserable thereby creating a situation where she is left with no other option but to leave her matrimonial house and compelling her to live in her parental home would also amount to cruelty.
8. The Supreme Court in the case of Rupali Devi v. State of U.P. and others, reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384 has held as under:
"14. "Cruelty" which is the crux of the offence under Section 498-A IPC is defined in Black's Law Dictionary to mean "the intentional and malicious infliction of mental or physical suffering on a living creature, esp. a human; abusive treatment; outrage (abuse, inhuman treatment, indignity)". Cruelty can be both physical or mental cruelty. The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma of being driven away from the Kapil Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25534528/
3 matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of being ill- treated are aspects that cannot be ignored while understanding the meaning of the expression "cruelty" appearing in Section 498-A of the Penal Code. The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home. Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home,
there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the husband including verbal exchanges, if any, that had compelled the wife to leave the matrimonial home and take shelter with her parents would continue to persist at the parental home. Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place."
9. This Court in the case of Amar Singh Vs. Smt. Vimla decided on 22.06.2021 in Criminal Revision No.2376/2020 (Gwalior Bench) reported in AIR Online 2021 M.P. 756 has held that compelling a married woman to live in her parental home also amounts to cruelty. 
10. There are specific allegations of demand of dowry and passing taunts by applicants Nos.2 & 3. 
The Supreme Court in the case of Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held as under:-
"12. In Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P. [Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P., (2014) 16 SCC 551], it was observed (SCC p. 553, paras 8-9):
"8. We have gone through the FIR and the criminal complaint. In the FIR, the appellants have not been named and in the criminal complaint they have been named without attributing any specific role to them. The relationship of the appellants with the husband of the complainant is distant. In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab [Kans Raj v.
State of Punjab, (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662] it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5):
"5. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in- laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits. In their overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case." 
The Court has, thus, to be careful in summoning distant relatives without there being specific material. Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations. Mere naming of distant relations is not enough to Kapil Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25534528/
4 summon them in the absence of any specific role and material to support such role. 
9. The parameters for quashing proceedings in a criminal complaint are well known. If there are triable issues, the Court is not expected to go into the veracity of the rival versions but where on the face of it, the criminal proceedings are abuse of Court's process, quashing jurisdiction can be exercised. Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar [K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar, (2000) 8 SCC 547 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 27] , Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate [Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 :
 1998 SCC (Cri) 1400] , State of  Haryana v. Bhajan Lal [State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 :
1992 SCC (Cri) 426 : AIR 1992 SC 604] and Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P.
[Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P., (2011) 11 SCC 259 : (2011) 3 SCC (Cri) 159] "
13. In the present case, the complaint is as follows: "Sir, it is submitted that I was married on 18-11- 2009 with Sidharath Parakh s/o Manak Chand Parakh r/o Sarafa Bazar in front of Radha Krishna Market, Gwalior according to the Hindu rites and customs. In the marriage my father had given gold and silver ornaments, cash amount and household goods according to his capacity. After the marriage when I went to my matrimonial home, I was treated nicely by the members of the family. 
When on the second occasion I went to my matrimonial home, my husband,
father-in-law and mother-in- law started harassing me for not bringing the dowry and started saying that I should bring from my father 25-30 tolas of gold and Rs 2,00,000 in cash and only then they would keep me in the house otherwise not. On account of this my husband also used to beat me and my father-in-law and my mother-in-law used to torture me by giving the taunts. In this connection I used to tell my father Kundanmal Oswal, my mother Smt Prem Lata Oswal, uncle Ashok Rai Sharma and uncle Ved Prakash Mishra from time to time. On 2-4- 2010 the members of the family of my matrimonial home forcibly sent me to the house of my parents in Ganj Basoda along with my brother Deepak. They snatched my clothes and ornaments and kept with them. Since then till today my husband has been harassing me on the telephone and has not come to take me back. Being compelled, I have been moving this application before you. Sir, it is prayed that action be taken against husband Sidharath Parakh, my father-in- law Manak Chand Parakh and my mother-in-law Smt Indira Parakh for torturing me on account of demanding dowry. 
14. From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out. There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home. Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home. The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with Kapil Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25534528/
5 cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out. 
Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible."
11. If the allegations made against applicant No.4/Rahul Gupta are considered, then it is clear that applicant No.4 is also residing in the same house. It is specifically mentioned by respondent No.2 in her FIR that her elder brother-in-law (Jaith) is also in habit of abusing her filthily. There are general allegations that all the applicants were demanding four-wheeler and on account of non-fulfillment of their demand, they were treating her with cruelty. It is true that for prosecuting the near and dear relatives of husband of complaint, the allegations are required to be specific but abusing the complainant on account of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry will also amount to specific allegation. This Court in exercise of power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. cannot dwell upon the correctness of the allegations and the proceedings can be quashed only if uncontroverted allegations do not make out an offence. 
12. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference. 
13. The application fails and is hereby dismissed.
